I joined my colleagues to introduce the Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act to ban the use of AI to prevent election fraud. We must protect our access to the ballot box!
Artificial intelligence is a huge threat to our elections. From fake robocalls to AI-generated content, it’s become much easier to spread disinformation and mislead voters.
But buried nearly 300 pages into this bill is something quite shocking: a blanket, 10-year ban on States and local governments from regulating artificial intelligence.

That is why I authored the AI Civil Rights Act, the most comprehensive AI legislation introduced in the U.S. Congress, which ensures that artificial intelligence serves the public good, not private profit exclusively. The bill would ensure that the AI age does not supercharge the bias and discrimination already prevalent today.

We want to reap the benefits of AI. We want to have AI be used across our society, but we also want to protect against the harmful effects of AI if it is put in the wrong hands to be used for the wrong purposes.

But then after they bought all these coins and enriched the President of the United States, well, then the President said: Let's give them the coins; let's give them these advanced chips.

The term ‘‘false AI-generated election media’’ means text. image, audio, or video that— (A) is the product of a computational process that uses machine learning, natural language processing, artificial intelligence techniques, or other computational processing techniques of similar or greater complexity; and (B) either— (i) contains materially false information relating to— (I) the time, place, or manner of holding any applicable Federal election; or (II) the qualifications for or restrictions on voter eligibility for any such election; or (ii) falsely depicts an election official.

Except as provided in subsection (c), a person may not— (1) knowingly distribute false AI-generated election media described in subsection (a)(3)(B)(i) if such person— (A) knows such media contains materially false information described in such subsection; and (B) has the purpose of impeding or preventing another person from exercising the right to vote in an applicable Federal election; or (2) knowingly distribute false AI-generated election media described in subsection (a)(3)(B)(ii) if such person— (A) knows the depiction of the election official in such media is materially false; and (B) has the intent to— (i) intimidate or harass an election official; or (ii) deter another person from exercising the right to vote in an applicable Federal election.
